newsitem.title: UK: UK house prices up 0.3 pct in April - Halifax.
newsitem.headline: UK house prices up 0.3 pct in April - Halifax.

text.p: The pace of Britain's housing market recovery slowed down in April, when prices rose by a seasonally adjusted 0.3 percent, against a one percent increase in March, according to the Halifax Building Society.
Year-on-year, prices were up 6.6 percent compared to 7.2 percent in the previous month, the Halifax said.
Its monthly index was 218.7, against 218.0 in March and 205.1 in April 1996.
"Despite recent sharp rises in house prices in London, reported in our last quarterly bulletin, price increases elsewhere in the UK have been more moderate," it said.

Prices paid by first-time buyers rose again in April by one percent, against a rise of 1.8 percent reported last month. But the annual rate of inflation in this sector of the market was now six percent.

New house prices continued to fluctuate, and were currently 0.2 percent lower than a year ago. Although the latest new house price figures suggested a weak market, the current trend was stronger, with prices rising by around 1.5 percent since the end of last year.
The average price of a new house was 70,215 stg in April.
The Halifax said house price inflation in Britain was still forecast at seven percent for the fourth quarter of 1997.
On Wednesday Nationwide Building Society said house prices were up 0.4 percent in April, after a 1.6 percent increase in March.
